review.market_summary: Three themes matter right now. (1) Chip export controls are the strongest and most-covered signal (score +0.69, news volume 8.4). The US has blocked China's remote access to AI chips, added license requirements for five countries and put curbs on Asian data centers. China has promised 'necessary measures', which puts the US-China trade truce at risk. Most of this is already in some prices: NVDA is down 12.6% in five days and SMH, AMAT and LRCX are each down about 5%. AMD is the clear laggard. (2) The Fed has turned hawkish. It raised rates for the first time since 2023, Musalem is calling for several more hikes by spring, and the dollar is at a 19-month high. That favors the dollar more than duration trades, because hikes could flatten the curve and safe-haven buying supports long bonds. (3) Iran is escalating again: a tanker was struck in Hormuz, Iran hit US targets in Bahrain for the third time after a two-month lull, and a third US carrier has arrived. Even so, crude fell over the week (USO -1.8%), squeezed by the strong dollar and hawkish Fed. That makes oil a short-term bet on further escalation, not a trend trade. Defense stocks and broad index shorts are weak, crowded ways to express these themes. Overall: a few trades, sized modestly.
